title: Personal Credit Cards: Statement Credit Size and the Cardholder's Checking Relationship
content:
How many Personal Credit Cards points a statement credit uses depends on whether the cardholder keeps an active checking account with Piedmont Crescent Bank.

## Rule

- **Cardholder holds a PCB checking account in active status.** Because leftover points can later be sent to that account, the statement credit stops at the smaller of two figures, the card's unredeemed points or the points needed to cover the amount owed, and the card does not end up owing the cardholder money.
- **No active PCB checking account held.** The credit takes the whole of the card's unredeemed points.

The test looks at the cardholder's checking accounts on the bank's records; any one of them in active status is enough.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Active PCB checking held | Unredeemed points | Points covering the amount owed | Points applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | 22100 | 21437 | 21437 |
| yes | 9800 | 21437 | 9800 |
| no | 22100 | 21437 | 22100 |
| no | 9800 | 21437 | 9800 |

In the third row the credit exceeds the debt, leaving the card in credit; that is the outcome the rule accepts when no active checking account exists.
